content.title: About
content.content: Rye flour is a whole‑grain product made by grinding rye kernels. It has a dark colour, a slightly sour aroma and a dense texture. It is used in breads, flatbreads, pancakes and various traditional dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rye flour is a staple in Scandinavian and Eastern European cuisines.
Sourdough rye bread is considered healthier than wheat‑based bread.
Rye contains more fiber and minerals than wheat.
In Russia rye flour is often labeled by degree of milling such as “0”, “1”, etc.
Rye flour can be used to make traditional kvass.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety and helps maintain gut health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rye flour provides thiamine, niacin and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains magnesium, phosphorus, iron and zinc, important for bones, blood and immunity.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with wheat flour, rye raises blood sugar more slowly.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Phenolic compounds in rye help combat free radicals.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Rye flour contains gluten and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: It contains phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in excess.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to rye.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Rye flour is used for baking breads, flatbreads, pancakes, quick breads and as a thickener in sauces. It can be blended with wheat flour for a lighter crumb. Rye dough usually benefits from a long fermentation period.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store rye flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
